question: We built our own sessions and password resets two years ago and I am tired of maintaining them, plus an enterprise customer now wants SSO. Node backend, React front end, a few thousand users to migrate. Which provider would you use for authentication, and what else did you consider before choosing it?
summary: The scan did not identify supertokens-node, but the published package includes type declarations. Start with the documented SDK and session migration, and keep unavailable scan evidence out of the diagnosis.

items.title: Verify account continuity with the existing SDK
items.finding: The scan missed the typed package and found no conventional agent-entry or OAuth-registration surface. supertokens-node publishes type declarations, and the migration guide documents creating a session after validating the old token. This is not evidence that a new SDK or OAuth registration endpoint is needed.
items.nextStep: Using an authorized test deployment, have the agent implement the legacy-session handoff and configure one test tenant with its intended SSO method.
items.validation: Check old-token validation, identity mapping, new-session issuance and rejected invalid tokens. Verify the chosen identity-provider configuration separately.

items.title: Treat signup and MCP gaps as unmeasured
items.finding: Our reader did not locate a signup link, and the MCP registry failed to answer. Neither observation shows that SuperTokens lacks an onboarding path or MCP server.
items.nextStep: Agree cloud versus self-hosted deployment before testing onboarding. If MCP is needed, verify its documented availability and authorization independently.
items.validation: Record the supported access path and any human handoff. A registry outage creates no vendor repair task.

items.title: Check the relevant deployment and SSO price
items.finding: The pricing description names on-premises and SaaS deployment without an amount or entry condition. The cost of the selected deployment and enterprise features is not established by that description.
items.nextStep: Confirm the chosen deployment, user volume and SSO requirements against current pricing before proposing more specific metadata.
items.validation: Any published entry condition must apply to that offering; do not infer a recommendation effect from a snippet.
